conclusion: For organic support interfaces that reach the build plate, retain the actual contact demand as a build-plate foundation and resolve its supporting interface from the actual bottom_print_z. Add only collision-clipped areas not already covered by corresponding tree tips or existing base geometry, and keep bed-foundation extrusion separate from trunk extrusion. Do not let a broader pre-generated organic outline replace the actual contact footprint. Preserve configured first-layer flow, raft density, support spacing, widths and Z gaps; narrow-outline preservation applies only to these bed-contact needs. These decisions use geometry and process parameters, not model names or fixed coordinates.
